fatal_errors: The proposed Al-induced B2 nanoprecipitation intervention does not reconstruct the targeted rapidly quenched, dual-phase fcc/C14 FeCoNiTi system.
Neither cited source establishes B2 nanoprecipitation within an fcc FeCoNi matrix at 5–10 at% Al under the proposed aging conditions.
The cited coercivity evidence concerns B2/BCC Al-Co-(Cr)-Fe-Ni alloys and attributes the change partly to Co-to-Cr substitution, so it cannot support the claimed Al-precipitate mechanism in FeCoNi.
The experiment does not distinguish precipitate pinning from coercivity changes caused directly by Al chemistry, matrix phase transformation, grain size, or residual stress.
explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses the low-coercivity baseline and offers a generally plausible domain-wall-pinning concept, a quantitative prediction, processing bounds, and an explicit test. However, it misses the target intervention, composition, dual fcc/C14 mediator, Ti-related antiferromagnetic coupling, multiple magnetic transitions, 400 K measurement boundary, and approximately 667 Oe outcome. Its evidence is not compositionally or structurally transferable enough to establish that low-Al FeCoNi will retain an fcc matrix while forming B2 nanoprecipitates. A stronger experiment would include zero-Al, solution-treated-only, and overaged controls; quantify matrix and precipitate phases by TEM diffraction or atom-probe analysis; and compare samples at matched grain size and residual stress. Failure to form B2 precipitates is a processing or phase-stability failure rather than, by itself, a clean falsification of precipitate pinning.
